text:
marta: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands. Two things we heard from customers: they want "future-proof" deployments that tolerate model swaps and hardware heterogeneity, and they keep asking what our long-term moat is vs big cloud vendors. Can leadership unpack both?

ben: TL;DR: our moat is operational predictability + migration velocity. Clouds sell GPUs and models; we sell a deterministic serving contract (latency, cost, fallbacks). Future-proofing = APIs + strong model compatibility + migration playbooks.

hugo: For engineering planning: what do we mean by "model swaps"? Are we promising zero-downtime switches between architectures (e.g., fp16 -> int8, llama2 -> mix-of-experts)?

ben: Not magic zero-downtime for arbitrary architecture changes. Promise is: a supported migration path with canary rollout, automated KV cache warming, and fallback to a compatible variant. We'll document supported swap patterns (quantization, small model bumps, variant routing).

sara: Ops question: how do we communicate hardware heterogeneity limits to customers? Some orgs want to run on mixed GPU fleets, others want single-instance determinism.

lee: Operational guideline: we certify certain hardware families for Dedicated and Private (A100s, H100s, etc.). We support heterogeneous pools but SLA tiers will reflect the weakest link (or require explicit routing policies). We'll add a compatibility matrix to Console.

marta: On the go-to-market side, customers think model catalogs = product. How do we avoid being boxed as "just" a model access layer?

ben: Messaging: lead with outcomes and proofs. Example claim: "Redwood customers maintain p95 SLAs while cutting inference cost by X% vs naive hosting." Back claims with bench results + anonymized case studies. Keep the catalog as an enabling feature, not the headline.

hugo: Competitor angle: some rivals advertise "free model updates" and training bundles. We should be explicit: are we ever going to do training or lifecycle data services?

ben: No plans to become a training platform. We may partner with training/service providers, but our product roadmap stays serving-first: runtime, routing, observability, and migration.

sara: Customers also asked about regulatory future-proofing (data residency + audit). Do we have clear asks for Private vs Dedicated?

lee: Yes. Private = full control + audit logs + customer KMS; Dedicated = strong isolation and SLA but hosted control plane; Hosted = easiest on-ramp. We'll make short one-liners for field teams and add example buyer personas in the Sales Kit.

marta: Nice. Last: what operational metrics will we publish as proof points? Bench suites are great, but customers want SLOs and long-term reliability signals.

policy-bot: Reminder: SRE and Product will publish a public SLO summary (p50/p95/p99, uptime) and a benchmark appendix in Console > Docs. Draft due next Wednesday. :calendar:
